mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.5% compresses discount rates and boosts equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS < 0.5%, or the Rank IC for FEDFUNDS level is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 600, it signals a weakening economy and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of instances where HOUST < 600, or the Rank IC for HOUST threshold is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate (UNRATE > 0.3pp increase in 3 months) combined with a low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 0.5%) indicates an impending recession and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances where UNRATE > 0.3pp increase in 3 months AND FEDFUNDS < 0.5%, or the Rank IC for the interaction is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of strong industrial production growth (INDPRO > 1.5% monthly growth), the S&P 500 tends to have positive 20-day returns due to robust economic activity.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where INDPRO > 1.5% monthly growth, or the Rank IC for INDPRO growth is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising labor force (PAYEMS > 0.5% monthly growth) indicates improving economic conditions and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where PAYEMS > 0.5% monthly growth, or the Rank IC for PAYEMS growth is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the core inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) rises above 225.0 (index value), it signals accelerating inflation and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL > 225.0, or the Rank IC for CPIAUCSL threshold is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When consumer credit (RSAFS) grows rapidly (RSAFS > 1.5% monthly growth) and the federal funds rate is low (FEDFUNDS < 0.5%), it indicates an accommodative environment that leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where RSAFS > 1.5% monthly growth AND FEDFUNDS < 0.5%, or the Rank IC for the interaction is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of strong GDP growth (GDPC1 > 2.0% annualized growth), the S&P 500 tends to have positive 20-day returns due to robust economic expansion.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where GDPC1 > 2.0% annualized growth, or the Rank IC for GDPC1 growth is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
